requirement:
An item with no attachments has an empty list. A language may return empty
lists for every item.
rationale:
**Obligations in `requirements.sdk.outlines.attachments.empty`**
- An item with no attachments MUST have an empty list.
- "A language may return empty lists for every item" is a MAY. It imposes nothing to test.

**Tests reviewed**
- `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[bundled_languages_classify_only_their_attachment_syntax]` carries the {test} reference to this requirement.
- It has a `test.txt` case: source `# just text\n`, expected attachments `vec![]`. Plain-text outlining produces one `line` node per non-blank line (`src/outline/mod.rs#fn[plain_text]`). So this case has an item with no attachments, and the test is not vacuous.
- The test flattens every item's attachments and compares the result to the expected list. An empty expected list therefore asserts that every item in the source has an empty `attachments`.
- Every other language case also compares the exact set of attachments across all items. Any spurious attachment on an item that should have none would fail the test. The Markdown case, for example, expects only the two block comments, and the unfinished comment, the inline comment and the code-fenced comment must produce nothing.
- `outline_constructors_preserve_fields_and_replace_attachments` in `tests/outline_content.rs` also asserts `item.attachments.is_empty()` for a freshly constructed item. It carries no {test} reference to this requirement, and the plain-text case already covers the obligation, so this does not matter.

**Gaps**
None. A regression that gave an attachment-free item a non-empty list would be caught by the exact-match assertions. The type is a list, so no other "empty" representation exists.
